question.text: A Pure DOMESTIC AIF structure differs from a Pure OFFSHORE structure PRIMARILY in that:

answer.text: Pure domestic has foreign investors only; pure offshore has domestic investors only

Pure domestic is a SEBI-registered onshore AIF with domestic investors, investing in domestic investees; pure offshore has no Indian pooling — the pooling vehicle is entirely abroad, investing into India via FPI/FVCI/FDI
Pure domestic funds are not subject to SEBI regulations
Pure offshore funds must register with MCA in India

explanation.text: The Logic: Pure domestic = SEBI-registered onshore AIF, domestic investors, domestic investees. Pure offshore = pooling vehicle entirely abroad, SEBI (AIF) does not apply to the pool itself, investments into India via FPI/FVCI/FDI. The workbook's Table 6.1 captures this distinction. The Trap: Option A reverses investor geography. Options C and D are fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: Shared across XIX-A/B/C/D. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat III manager with pure domestic, you have a single SEBI/IMA/PPM stack to maintain — simpler compliance, but you miss the offshore capital pool. Decide based on your sponsor's capital pipeline.
